Is there a difference between TT and Tt? Just out of interest

TT is dominant, while Tt in recessive. If something is dominant, they will pass it on to their offspring 100%, with recessive it'd be lower in chances. Let's sayy we breed an ee/Aa/TT (tawny) to an ee/Aa/tt (brown) you have 0% of getting a brown, you will get a Tawny due to there being 2 Aa's which would either make a dom or a recessive, depending on if the admins would you RNG for that :3

It has been stated several times in the past yes, that breeding blacks to tawnies will never result in black puppies, regardless of whether the black is EE or Ee. Tokotas have their very own genetic system that is, for the most part, unrelated to other genetic systems in how the genes are passed.

I've taken these comments from the Breeding and Genotypes Guide , which is posted publicly to the group, where people have had similar confusions; 

 comments.deviantart.com/1/5586… 

 comments.deviantart.com/1/5586… 

And this comment, from the Genetics and Mutations journal which has been posted to the group since the very beginning:

 comments.deviantart.com/1/4612… 

As you can see, EE blacks do not guarantee the passing of E in any breeding. Since Tokotas are primarily meant to be a light-coloured species, breeding Black is designed to be harder than breeding, say, a Tundra or a Tawny. It's always a good idea to scroll through the comments of the genetics journals if you're unsure of something, as many others have likely had the same questions answered by the admins.

The owner can simply be notified and they can reply to the permission or breeding stating that the other person can post the litter. This is to help owners keep track of their Tokota's permissions and used breedings, as well as respect an owner's personal preference to whether or not they want to have their slots sold/gifted/traded/shared.
